title: Symfony
intro: Applies to: Symfony controllers, services, Messenger message handlers, console commands.

entries.rule: Services **MUST NOT** be fetched with `$container->get()`; they **MUST** be autowired through the constructor. This is the Symfony form of the no-service-location rule in `php-core.md` (`laravel-kanon` skill).

checks.coverage: Flags $container->get() calls in production classes.

entries.lane_note: Symfony overlay of PHP-001 (`php-core.md`).

entries.rule: Product modules **MUST NOT** depend on a `ContainerInterface` (a closed locator under SYM-005 excepted), and production classes **MUST** inject contracts (`LoggerInterface`, `ClockInterface`, `Security` in controllers only) instead of globals; `Framework\` is exempt.

checks.coverage: Fails a class outside `Framework\` that depends on `Psr\Container\ContainerInterface` or `Symfony\Component\DependencyInjection\ContainerInterface`. It over-flags a closed locator under SYM-005, so allow-list those classes.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-008, ORCH-010 (no facades or global helpers, where facades are allowed).

entries.rule: Credentials and config values **MUST** come from `%env(...)%` parameters or the secrets vault, and production classes **MUST NOT** call `getenv()` or read `$_ENV` or `$_SERVER` outside `Framework\`.

checks.coverage: Flags `getenv()`, `$_ENV` and `$_SERVER` reads outside `Framework\`.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: INT-011, PERS-007, ORCH-008 (env half).

entries.rule: A service locator with a closed, declared service list (`#[AutowireLocator]`, `getSubscribedServices()`) **MAY** be used for runtime selection such as a keyed strategy map; `->get()` on such a closed locator is not the container fetch SYM-001 bans.

checks.coverage: Narrow the SYM-001 detector so `->get()` on a `ServiceLocator` built by `#[AutowireLocator]` is not flagged.

entries.rule: CI **SHOULD** run `bin/console lint:container` so an unautowirable service fails at compile time, not on first request.
A query handler **MUST** stay pure (no cache reads or writes); caching **MUST** live in a middleware on `query.bus`, and logging around the handler **SHOULD** live there too.

checks.coverage: Classes with `#[AsMessageHandler(bus: 'query.bus')]` must not depend on `Symfony\Contracts\Cache\CacheInterface`.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-033, ORCH-036 (pure query handlers, logging in a decorator).

entries.rule: Cache keys, tags and TTLs **MUST** come from centralized enum or key classes, never raw strings or hardcoded integers.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-034 (centralized cache keys).

entries.rule: Writes **MUST** go through a Symfony Messenger command dispatched to one handler, so every write shares one transaction and validation path. This is the Symfony counterpart of the Laravel command/handler slice (`architecture.md` in the `laravel-kanon` skill).
entries.why: every write shares one transaction and validation path
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ARCH-005 (command/handler write slice) and ARCH-009 (explicit handler wiring) in `architecture.md`.

entries.rule: A read-only context (reporting projection, query layer) **MUST NOT** contain a message dispatched on `command.bus`, its handler, or a domain event it emits; it reacts to events with listeners and answers queries.

checks.coverage: Fails a `*Command` class or a `command.bus` handler inside a namespace on a read-only list (the list is configuration; event dispatch is not visible to the check).

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ARCH-003, ARCH-012 (read-only contexts, no write command in reporting).

entries.rule: Every capability **MUST** ship as a vertical slice (message, handler, `*Controller`, `*Request`, `*Resource` in one folder), and a module **SHOULD NOT** group slices under domain folders (`Lifecycle/`, `Queries/`) before about ten slices; names carry the suffix `{Action}Command`, `{Action}Query`, `{Action}CommandHandler`, `{Action}QueryHandler`, `{Action}Controller`, `{Action}Request`, `{Action}Resource` or `{Action}ConsoleCommand`, with no `*Job`.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ARCH-005, ARCH-010 (vertical slice, no premature grouping), plus the suffix note.

entries.rule: Slice pieces **MUST** be co-located in that slice's folder, and code **MUST NOT** be scattered across type-named folders (`Controller/`, `Request/`, `Resource/`, `Enum/`, `Event/`, `Entity/`, `Repository/`, `Message/`, `Dto/`) inside a module.

checks.coverage: Fails a class whose namespace has one of those segments inside a module outside `Framework\`.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ARCH-006, ARCH-007 (folder half) (co-location, entity concept folders).

entries.rule: Every command and query **MUST** have exactly one handler, bound to its bus explicitly with `#[AsMessageHandler(bus: 'command.bus')]` or `#[AsMessageHandler(bus: 'query.bus')]`; Messenger has no option enforcing one handler, so a check fails a message handled twice.

checks.coverage: Custom rule: a handler class without `#[AsMessageHandler(bus: ...)]`, or one message class handled by two handlers, fails. Messenger has no bus option for this.
A class with `#[AsMessageHandler]` must name a bus (HaveAttribute exists; the one-handler count needs a custom expression).

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ARCH-009, PERS-009 (explicit handler wiring, no auto-discovery).

entries.rule: A message handler **MUST NOT** be a pass-through whose body only dispatches an event with no preceding mutation.

checks.coverage: Custom rule on the `__invoke()` body (does not exist yet): body is one `dispatch()` call with no write before it.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ISO-013 (no pass-through handler).

entries.rule: Application-layer classes (handlers, listeners, console commands) **MUST** be orchestrators that resolve dependencies, delegate to an entity or domain-service method, and dispatch; they **MUST NOT** hold business logic, mutate entity state directly, create related rows inline, or call an external system directly; guard clauses and payload parsing **MAY** stay.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-001 to ORCH-004 (orchestrator pattern).

entries.rule: Controllers, handlers, listeners, messages (`*Command`, `*Query`), events, `*Request` and `*Resource` DTOs **MUST** be `final readonly class`; entities and console commands extending a non-readonly base **MAY** drop `readonly`.
allowed_in: Console commands extending a non-readonly base

checks.coverage: Classes with these suffixes must be final and readonly; skip classes with `#[ORM\Entity]`.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-012 (final readonly classes).

entries.rule: A message handler **MUST** be named `{Action}CommandHandler` or `{Action}QueryHandler` and expose exactly one public method, `__invoke(Message)`.

checks.coverage: Handler classes match `*CommandHandler` or `*QueryHandler` (HaveNameMatching); the single public method needs a custom expression.
Custom rule: exactly one public method, named `__invoke`.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-019 (one public handler method).

entries.rule: A query handler **MUST** return a typed `*Result` DTO, never an array, and a command handler **MUST** return nothing (`void`), so the caller creates the id and puts it in the command.

checks.coverage: Return type of `__invoke` on `query.bus` handlers is a class, not `array`; on `command.bus` handlers it is `void`.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-020 (typed Result DTOs).

entries.rule: Domain events **MUST** be dispatched from the application layer on `event.bus`, and an entity **MUST NOT** dispatch events or receive an `EventDispatcherInterface` or a message bus.

checks.coverage: Classes with `#[ORM\Entity]` must not depend on `EventDispatcherInterface`, `MessageBusInterface`, `CommandBus` or `QueryBus`.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-026 (events from the application layer).

entries.rule: Audit and history records **MUST NOT** be written inline in handlers or entity methods; a state change **MUST** dispatch a domain event and a dedicated `final readonly` listener on `event.bus` **MUST** record it.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-027 (audit through a listener).

entries.rule: Mail **MUST** be sent from a listener through `MailerInterface`, with `SendEmailMessage` routed to the async transport, never inline from a handler.

checks.coverage: Classes depending on `MailerInterface` must be listeners.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-028 (mail through a queued listener).

entries.rule: Messages and events **MUST NOT** hold Doctrine entities; they **MUST** carry ids, scalars, value objects or a small DTO.

checks.coverage: Message and event classes must not depend on classes with `#[ORM\Entity]` (PHPStan custom rule is the alternative for constructor types).

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-032, MD-022 (jobs and events carry ids, not models).

entries.rule: Events **MUST** be past-tense facts dispatched on `event.bus` with `DispatchAfterCurrentBusStamp`, so listeners run after the command's transaction commits and never run if the handler throws.
entries.why: so listeners run after the command's transaction commits and never run if the handler throws

checks.coverage: Event naming per the owner's call (D22); the stamp itself is not visible to PHPArkitect.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-021 (past-tense events, after the state change).

entries.rule: Events **MUST** be `final readonly`, constructor only, with no query or business helper methods.

checks.coverage: Custom rule: an event class declares no method besides the constructor.
Event classes are final and readonly; skip `#[ORM\Entity]`.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-023 (events are pure data).

entries.rule: Commands, queries and events **MUST** use separate Messenger buses (`command.bus`, `query.bus`, `event.bus`), each with its own middleware.
The event bus **MUST** set `allow_no_handlers: true` and register one `#[AsMessageHandler(bus: 'event.bus')]` handler per listener.

The command bus **SHOULD** include the `validation` middleware, with `Assert` constraints on command classes that no `*Request` validates (console, scheduler, consumers), so a constraint is declared once and invalid input never reaches a handler.

Every write **MUST** run in one transaction opened by the `doctrine_transaction` middleware on `command.bus`; handlers, controllers, aggregates and domain services **MUST NOT** open, commit or flush a transaction themselves.

checks.coverage: Flags `flush()`, `wrapInTransaction()`, `beginTransaction()` and `commit()` calls in handlers, controllers, entities and domain services.

entries.rule: A `catch (DomainException)` around `dispatch()` **MUST NOT** be used, because Messenger wraps handler exceptions in `HandlerFailedException`; code dispatching on a synchronous bus **MUST** unwrap it so the domain exception reaches the exception listener.
entries.why: so the domain exception reaches the exception listener
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-024 (second sentence only).

entries.rule: A handler **MUST NOT** populate an entity from a command or request DTO wholesale (serializer `OBJECT_TO_POPULATE`, ObjectMapper, array hydration); it **MUST** list the fields it writes.

checks.coverage: Custom rule: flag `OBJECT_TO_POPULATE`, `ObjectMapperInterface::map()` and array hydration inside handler classes.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-015 (no validated() spread into create or update).

entries.rule: Controllers **MUST NOT** extend `AbstractController`; a `readonly` class cannot extend the non-readonly `AbstractController`, so a controller injects any service it needs explicitly.
entries.why: a `readonly` class cannot extend the non-readonly `AbstractController`

checks.coverage: Fails a class named *Controller that extends Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-013 (no framework base controller).

entries.rule: Controllers **MUST** be single-action (`__invoke()` only) with `#[Route]` on the class, never multi-action controllers.

checks.coverage: A custom expression fails a *Controller class with a public method other than __invoke; no built-in method-count expression exists.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-018 (single-action controllers).

entries.rule: A controller **MUST NOT** call or inject another controller, including through `forward()`; shared work moves into a handler that both controllers call through a bus.

checks.coverage: Fails a *Controller class that depends on another *Controller class.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-022 (controller does not call controller).

entries.rule: Each user intent **MUST** have its own route, and an endpoint **MUST NOT** pick its action from the request body.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-002 (one route per intent).

entries.rule: Every route **MUST** be named `{module}.{resource}.{action}` through `#[Route(name:)]`; thin public one-off routes **MAY** use a single-segment name.

checks.coverage: A custom rule reads the #[Route] attribute and fails a missing or non-matching name argument.

examples.bad:
#[Route('/api/orders', methods: ['POST'])]
final readonly class CreateOrderController {}
examples.good:
#[Route('/api/orders', name: 'commerce.orders.create', methods: ['POST'])]
final readonly class CreateOrderController {}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-003 (route naming).

entries.rule: Route parameters **MUST** be plain ids resolved inside the handler, and `#[MapEntity]` or an entity-typed controller argument **MUST NOT** be used.

checks.coverage: Fails a *Controller class that depends on a class carrying #[ORM\Entity]; whether attribute arguments count as dependencies was not checked.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-004 (no route-model binding).

entries.rule: Controllers **MUST NOT** call `persist()` or `flush()` and **SHOULD NOT** hold business rules; they turn the request into a command, dispatch it, and build the response.

checks.coverage: Fails a *Controller class that depends on Doctrine\ORM\EntityManagerInterface. It does not see business rules in the controller.

entries.rule: Each module **MUST** own its route file (`<module>-routes.php`), imported from `modules.php` with its `/api` prefix declared there.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-001 (route file per module).

entries.rule: Abuse-prone endpoints (login, signup, email resend, password reset) **MUST** be rate limited: `login_throttling` on the login firewall, `#[RateLimit]` on the others.
applies_to: login, signup, email resend and password reset endpoints

examples.bad:
#[Route('/api/password-resets', name: 'identity.password_resets.create', methods: ['POST'])]
final readonly class RequestPasswordResetController {}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-007 (throttle on abuse-prone endpoints).

entries.rule: HTTP input **MUST** be a `*Request` DTO bound with `#[MapRequestPayload]` or `#[MapQueryString]` and validated with `#[Assert\...]` constraints, never an inline `$validator->validate()` call; `#[MapQueryString]` **MUST** set `validationFailedStatusCode: 422` because it defaults to 404, and authorization **MUST NOT** live in the DTO.

checks.coverage: Flags ValidatorInterface injected into a *Controller class; it does not check which constraints a *Request carries.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-025 (validation in request classes).

entries.rule: Each write action **MUST** have its own `*Request` DTO, and a `*Request` **MUST NOT** serve several actions.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-009 (one request class per write action).

entries.rule: Every field the handler reads **MUST** be a required constructor parameter of the `*Request`, or optional with a default written in the constructor signature; a handler-read field **MUST NOT** be optional by accident (an uninitialized property).
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-010 (fields required or explicit default).

entries.rule: Fields an endpoint ignores **SHOULD** be rejected with `AbstractNormalizer::ALLOW_EXTRA_ATTRIBUTES => false` in the payload `serializationContext`, so clients get a 422 instead of a silent success.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-011 (ignored fields prohibited).

entries.rule: Date inputs **MUST** use an explicit format, `#[Assert\Date]` on a `Y-m-d` string or `DateTimeNormalizer::FORMAT_KEY` in the payload `serializationContext`, never the loose default parser.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-012 (explicit date format).

entries.rule: Client-chosen sort and filter fields **MUST** arrive as backed-enum `*Request` properties mapped to columns you chose to expose; raw input **MUST NOT** reach `orderBy()`, `addOrderBy()` or `where()` as a field name.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-013 (sort and filter columns via enum).

entries.rule: A `#[Assert\...]` constraint **MUST** stay on the `*Request` property even when a value object also enforces it, so form users get a field-level 422 instead of a 500.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-014 (field rule stays when a value object enforces it).

entries.rule: Create **MUST** return 201 (`Response::HTTP_CREATED`); a create that returns 200 is a violation.

examples.bad:
$this->commands->dispatch(new CreateOrderCommand($id, $request->customerId, $request->quantity));

return new JsonResponse(new OrderCreatedResource($id));

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-016 (create returns 201).

entries.rule: State changes and deletes **MUST** return 204 with no body; reads return 200.

examples.bad:
$this->commands->dispatch(new CancelOrderCommand($id));

return new JsonResponse(['status' => 'cancelled']);
examples.good:
$this->commands->dispatch(new CancelOrderCommand($id));

return new Response(null, Response::HTTP_NO_CONTENT);

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-017 (state changes and deletes return 204).

entries.rule: Controllers **MUST** return a `*Resource` in a `JsonResponse` or `Response` with an explicit status, and **MUST NOT** hand-assemble arrays; dedicated `*Resource` classes build the body.

checks.coverage: A custom rule flags an array literal passed to JsonResponse in a *Controller class and a __invoke return type other than Response.

examples.bad:
$result = $this->queries->ask(new GetOrderQuery($id));

return new JsonResponse(['id' => $result->id, 'total' => $result->totalCents]);
examples.good:
$result = $this->queries->ask(new GetOrderQuery($id));

return new JsonResponse(OrderResource::fromResult($result), Response::HTTP_OK);

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-023, HTTP-018 (typed resource with explicit status).

entries.rule: A `*Resource` **MUST NOT** map a nested collection inline; nested relations **MUST** get their own `*Resource` class.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-019 (no manual collection map in a resource).

entries.rule: A `*Resource` **MUST** be built from the typed Result DTO the handler returns through `QueryBus::ask()`, never from array keys.

examples.bad:
$data = $this->queries->ask(new GetOrderQuery($id));

return new JsonResponse(new OrderResource($data['id'], $data['total']), Response::HTTP_OK);

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-020 (resource reads typed properties).

entries.rule: Response keys **MUST** be snake_case, a single object **MUST** be wrapped in `data`, collections **MUST** add `meta` and `links`, and errors **MUST** use the RFC 7807 problem details shape Symfony emits (`type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`).
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-021 (response envelope and keys).

entries.rule: Dates **MUST** serialize as ISO 8601 with `format(\DATE_ATOM)` or the default `DateTimeNormalizer`.

examples.bad: return ['data' => ['created_at' => $this->createdAt->format('d/m/Y H:i')]];
examples.good: return ['data' => ['created_at' => $this->createdAt->format(\DATE_ATOM)]];

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-022 (ISO 8601 dates).

entries.rule: Every API controller **MUST** carry attribute-driven OpenAPI documentation (`#[OA\Response]` and the like), with a matching `#[OA\Parameter]` for every route parameter.

checks.coverage: A custom rule fails a #[Route] controller with no #[OA\...] attribute and a route parameter with no #[OA\Parameter].

examples.bad:
#[Route('/api/orders/{id}', name: 'commerce.orders.show', methods: ['GET'])]
final readonly class ShowOrderController {}
examples.good:
#[Route('/api/orders/{id}', name: 'commerce.orders.show', methods: ['GET'])]
#[OA\Parameter(name: 'id', in: 'path', required: true, schema: new OA\Schema(type: 'string'))]
#[OA\Response(response: 200, description: 'The order', content: new OA\JsonContent(ref: new Model(type: OrderResource::class)))]
final readonly class ShowOrderController {}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-024, HTTP-026 (documented endpoints, route parameters).

entries.rule: The documented response example **MUST** match the `*Resource` output shape, with realistic data.

examples.bad:
// OrderResource emits data.order_id and data.total_cents
#[OA\Response(response: 200, content: new OA\JsonContent(example: ['id' => 'string', 'total' => 0]))]

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-025 (documented example matches the resource).

entries.rule: Webhook routes **MUST** live in their own route file (or be mounted by the Webhook component), behind signature verification, on an entry open to the provider (`PUBLIC_ACCESS`), and **MUST NOT** sit behind user authentication.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-027 (webhook routes).

entries.rule: Webhook processing **MUST** be dispatched to an async transport and **MUST** be idempotent: check an idempotency key against a tracking record first, no-op on repeats, and record the outcome so the tracking record always settles.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-028 (webhook processing queued and idempotent).

entries.rule: Controllers **MUST NOT** try/catch domain exceptions; each module **MUST** have a base `*Exception`, and its concrete domain exceptions extend it and carry `#[WithHttpStatus]` so they render themselves.

checks.coverage: Fails a product *Exception class that is not a RuntimeException and carries neither #[WithHttpStatus] nor HttpExceptionInterface.
A custom rule flags a try/catch block inside a *Controller class.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-024, MD-029, AUTH-004 (controllers do not catch, module base exception).

entries.rule: A message handler **MUST** receive the acting user as a field of its command and **MUST NOT** read `Security` or `TokenStorageInterface`; the controller takes the actor from the authenticated principal, never from the request body.

checks.coverage: Fails a class named *Handler that depends on Symfony\Bundle\SecurityBundle\Security or TokenStorageInterface.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-021 (actor passed on the command).

entries.rule: Every endpoint touching owned data **MUST** authorize the actor against the loaded entity with a Voter, checked in the handler through `AuthorizationCheckerInterface`; the controller **MUST** build the command's actor from the same authenticated token the Voter reads, which is why the handler runs on the synchronous bus, and a handler **MUST NOT** use `find()` plus a hand-written ownership check.
applies_to: endpoints and handlers that touch owned data

checks.coverage: A custom rule flags EntityRepository::find() called inside a *Handler class. It over-flags handlers that read ownerless data.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: AUTH-002, AUTH-003 (actor-scoped lookup, ownership gate).

entries.rule: The authorization gate **MUST** throw a product `*Exception` carrying `#[WithHttpStatus(403)]` (or a Voter denial raising `AccessDeniedException`), and controllers **MUST NOT** build 403 responses inline.

checks.coverage: A custom rule flags the 403 status passed to a Response or JsonResponse inside a *Controller class.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: AUTH-004 (gate throws, renders as 403).

entries.rule: Capability-gated endpoints **MUST** use `#[IsGranted]` with a class constant or a backed-enum `->value`, never a string literal.

checks.coverage: A custom rule flags #[IsGranted] whose first argument is a string literal.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: AUTH-006, HTTP-008 (typed capability constant).

entries.rule: State-changing and owned-data routes **MUST** require authentication through `access_control` or `#[IsGranted('IS_AUTHENTICATED_FULLY')]`; only genuinely public reads **MAY** use `PUBLIC_ACCESS`.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: HTTP-006 (auth group for state-changing and owned-data routes).

entries.rule: Once a product has a second application, each application surface **MUST** authenticate through its own firewall and user provider, and firewalls and role enums are never shared.
applies_to: products with a second application surface

checks.coverage: A layer rule bars the admin layer from depending on the customer role enums. It does not see the firewall wiring.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: AUTH-007, ISO-014 (separate guard per application).

entries.rule: Business logic **MUST** live in entity methods (invariants and state transitions), finders **MUST NOT** live on the entity, entities **SHOULD NOT** expose public setters that skip the rules, and logic spanning several aggregates **MUST** live in a handler.

checks.coverage: Classes with #[ORM\Entity] must not depend on EntityManagerInterface or a *Repository.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-006 (business logic in model methods).

entries.rule: A command handler **SHOULD** save one aggregate; other aggregates **SHOULD** be updated by a listener on `event.bus` that reacts to a domain event dispatched with `DispatchAfterCurrentBusStamp`.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-007 (one aggregate per transaction).

entries.rule: Collection associations **MUST** be typed `Collection` with generics (`Collection<int, OrderLine>`).

checks.coverage: Level max with phpstan-doctrine reports a Collection without generics.

examples.bad:
#[ORM\OneToMany(targetEntity: OrderLine::class, mappedBy: 'order')]
private Collection $lines;

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-004 (relationship return types).

entries.rule: Entities and custom Doctrine types **MUST NOT** run queries or depend on `EntityManagerInterface` or a repository; derived values **MUST** be computed from data already loaded.

checks.coverage: Classes with #[ORM\Entity] must not depend on Doctrine\ORM\EntityManagerInterface or a *Repository.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-009 (accessors and casts run no queries).

entries.rule: A read model **MUST** be strictly read-only: a `final readonly` DTO built by a query handler, or an `#[ORM\Entity(readOnly: true)]` over a table the module does not write; mutations belong to the write entity.

checks.coverage: Read-model classes must be `final readonly` DTOs or carry `#[ORM\Entity(readOnly: true)]`; any other `#[ORM\Entity]` among read models is flagged.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-015 (read models read-only).

entries.rule: Handlers and entities **MUST NOT** throw `\RuntimeException` or Symfony HTTP exceptions for business rules; they **MUST** throw a named product exception.

checks.coverage: Custom rule: a handler or entity throws a generic or framework exception.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-032 (no framework or generic exceptions for business rules).

entries.rule: Domain and application classes **MUST NOT** import `HttpFoundation`, `HttpKernel` or `Doctrine\` types, except ORM mapping attributes and `Collection` on entities, `#[WithHttpStatus]` on product exceptions and `Doctrine\DBAL\Connection` in read-model query classes (SYM-074, SYM-076); each vendor SDK or HTTP client **MUST** sit behind an interface with an adapter (the Doctrine repository is that adapter), while Symfony attributes, `Assert` constraints, Messenger, Uid and PSR contracts **MAY** be imported.

checks.coverage: Domain and application namespaces must not depend on `Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation`, `Symfony\Component\HttpKernel` or `Doctrine\`, except ORM mapping attributes, `Collection`, `#[WithHttpStatus]` and `Doctrine\DBAL\Connection` in read-model query classes; vendor SDK namespaces are allowed only in the adapter.

entries.rule: A lookup by id **MUST** go through a repository method that throws a product exception when the row is missing, mapped to 404 with `#[WithHttpStatus(404)]`; callers **MUST NOT** `find()` and null-check the result.

checks.coverage: Custom rule on the result of EntityManagerInterface::find() used with a null check (does not exist yet).

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-006 (lookups throw on missing) and MD-030 (no custom not-found for a plain lookup).

entries.rule: A module **MUST NOT** add columns to another module's tables; it **MUST** create its own table keyed by the other module's id.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ISO-006 (modules own their tables).

entries.rule: Cross-module data access that is not materialized under SYM-104 **MUST** be read-only, through an injected `Doctrine\DBAL\Connection` inside a repository or read-model query with id-based queries; a module **MUST NOT** insert, update or delete rows in another module's tables.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ISO-007 (cross-module reads are read-only).

entries.rule: Once a second application exists, each application **MUST** own its read models (entities mapped `#[ORM\Entity(readOnly: true)]`), its write models and its enums.
applies_to: products with more than one application
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ISO-010 (each application owns its read and write models).

entries.rule: Queries **MUST** go through a repository and fetch-join what they iterate; production classes outside repositories and read-model queries **MUST NOT** depend on DBAL `Connection`.

checks.coverage: Production classes outside repositories must not depend on Doctrine\DBAL\Connection.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-010 (queries via the model, eager-load what you iterate).

entries.rule: A query rule used by more than one handler **SHOULD** live in one Specification or one named repository method instead of being repeated.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-011 (Specification or scope for shared query rules).

entries.rule: A Doctrine lifecycle callback or entity listener **MUST NOT** call `flush()` or `persist()` for the entity that triggered it; decide every field first and write once.

checks.coverage: Custom rule: flush( inside a lifecycle callback method or an entity listener class.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-008 (observers must not re-save the row).

entries.rule: Publicly exposed identifiers **MUST NOT** be enumerable auto-increment integers; ids **MUST** be ULIDs or UUIDv7 created by the caller.

examples.bad:
#[ORM\Id]
#[ORM\GeneratedValue]
#[ORM\Column]
private ?int $id = null;

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-014 (non-enumerable public ids) and PERS-005 (non-enumerable primary keys).

entries.rule: A Doctrine migration **MUST** implement a `down()` that reverses it, or call `throwIrreversibleMigrationException()` with a note.

checks.coverage: Custom rule: empty down() body with no throwIrreversibleMigrationException() call.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: PERS-001 (migration down()).

entries.rule: PHP FQCNs **MUST NOT** be stored in database columns (defaults, seeds, discriminator values); use plain string identifiers.

examples.bad:
#[ORM\Entity]
#[ORM\InheritanceType('SINGLE_TABLE')]
#[ORM\DiscriminatorColumn(name: 'type', type: 'string')]
#[ORM\DiscriminatorMap([Card::class => Card::class, BankTransfer::class => BankTransfer::class])]
abstract class Payment
{
}
examples.good:
#[ORM\Entity]
#[ORM\InheritanceType('SINGLE_TABLE')]
#[ORM\DiscriminatorColumn(name: 'type', type: 'string')]
#[ORM\DiscriminatorMap(['card' => Card::class, 'bank_transfer' => BankTransfer::class])]
abstract class Payment
{
}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: PERS-002 (no FQCN in columns).

entries.rule: Lifecycle state **MUST** be a string column mapped to a backed enum with an index, never a boolean flag.

examples.bad:
#[ORM\Column]
private bool $isActive = true;

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: PERS-003 (status string column cast to a backed enum).

entries.rule: Doctrine-backed repositories **SHOULD** implement a domain interface by wrapping `EntityManagerInterface`, not extend `ServiceEntityRepository`, so `find*` is not public; `add()` **SHOULD** only `persist()`, because the `doctrine_transaction` middleware on `command.bus` flushes.

checks.coverage: Classes named *Repository must not extend ServiceEntityRepository.

entries.rule: Every external system **MUST** sit behind a dedicated gateway class owned by the integrating module, one per vendor, with domain-language methods and typed DTOs; handlers, listeners and controllers **MUST NOT** call a vendor SDK or `HttpClientInterface` directly.

checks.coverage: *Handler, *Listener and *Controller classes must not depend on HttpClientInterface or a vendor SDK namespace.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: INT-001 (gateway per vendor).

entries.rule: A decoded external payload **MUST** become a typed DTO once, at the edge, before any other code reads it.

checks.coverage: Custom rule: json_decode( on a request body outside Framework\.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: INT-004 (typed DTO at the edge).

entries.rule: HTTP integrations **MUST** use one scoped `HttpClient` per vendor, with base URL, timeouts and retry set in config and injected with `#[Target]`.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: INT-005 (one connector per vendor) and INT-007 (explicit timeouts and retry).

entries.rule: A parameter default for a vendor host **SHOULD** point at the real production host, not a placeholder.

examples.bad: $container->parameters()->set('acme_pay.base_uri', 'https://example.com');
examples.good: $container->parameters()->set('acme_pay.base_uri', 'https://api.acme-pay.com');

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: INT-012 (config default points at the real host).

entries.rule: A class that needs config values **SHOULD** receive them as typed constructor parameters with `#[Autowire(param: ...)]`, not through `ParameterBagInterface`.

checks.coverage: Product classes must not depend on ParameterBagInterface.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: INT-013 (typed constructor config).

entries.rule: Outbound effects triggered by domain changes **MUST** hang off domain events handled by listeners on `event.bus`, so the integration can be replayed, retried or removed without touching domain code.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: INT-015 (outbound effects hang off domain events).

entries.rule: Time-consuming or external work (HTTP calls, mail, heavy processing) **MUST** run in an asynchronous Messenger handler on a routed transport, never synchronously in a handler or controller.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-029 (slow or external work in the queue), INT-014 (external calls in queued jobs).

entries.rule: Every asynchronous message **MUST** be routed to a named transport explicitly (`#[AsMessage('async')]` or `framework.messenger.routing`), never left to a default or a fallback.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-030 (explicit queue per job).

entries.rule: A transport carrying messages that call external systems (webhooks included) **MUST** declare an explicit `retry_strategy` and a `failure_transport`.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-031 (tries and backoff on external jobs), HTTP-029 (explicit tries and backoff on webhook jobs).

entries.rule: Handlers **SHOULD** throw `UnrecoverableMessageHandlingException` for failures a retry cannot fix and `RecoverableMessageHandlingException` to force a retry.

Handlers in a long-running Messenger worker **SHOULD** load their entities by id on every call and keep none in properties, because the worker clears the entity manager after each message (`DoctrineClearEntityManagerWorkerSubscriber` from the Doctrine bridge).
A query **MUST NOT** load a whole table and filter it in PHP (`findAll()` then `array_filter()`); the condition **MUST** go into the DQL or `QueryBuilder`.

checks.coverage: Custom rule: flags findAll() called on a repository in product code.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: PERF-001 (filter in the database).

entries.rule: Filtering on an association **SHOULD** use a DQL join, an `EXISTS` subquery or `COUNT` so the database decides; fetching every association row to filter in PHP **SHOULD NOT** be used.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: PERF-002 (filter on a relation in the database).

entries.rule: A mapping **MUST NOT** declare `fetch: 'EAGER'` on an association; associations **MUST** be loaded per query with a fetch join (`SELECT o, l FROM Billing\Order\Order o JOIN o.lines l`).

checks.coverage: Custom rule: flags fetch: 'EAGER' in #[ORM\OneToMany], #[ORM\ManyToOne], #[ORM\OneToOne] and #[ORM\ManyToMany] arguments. PHPArkitect cannot read attribute arguments.

examples.bad:
#[ORM\OneToMany(targetEntity: OrderLine::class, mappedBy: 'order', fetch: 'EAGER')]
private Collection $lines; // loaded on every query, read or not

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: PERF-003 (no `$with` default).

entries.rule: List and report queries **SHOULD** select only the columns they use (`SELECT NEW ResultClass(...)` or a scalar select), and an aggregate report **SHOULD** be one `GROUP BY` query, never a PHP loop over entities.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: PERF-005, PERF-006 (select needed columns, aggregate in one query).

entries.rule: Product code **MUST** be organised into modules listed in `modules.php`, one root namespace per business capability (`Billing\`, `Orders\`), not into framework-type namespaces (`Service\`, `Repository\`, `Action\`) at the product root.

checks.coverage: Fails a class in a Service, Repository or Action namespace outside Framework\, or in a root namespace missing from modules.php.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ARCH-001 (modules, not type folders).

entries.rule: A module **MUST NOT** import another module's classes (entities, enums, messages, handlers, services or value objects), except a published domain event and an interface the consuming module owns that the providing module implements (SYM-102); `Framework\` is allowed from every module.
allowed_in: pure infrastructure in the shared `Framework\` namespace
an interface the consuming module owns that the providing module implements

checks.coverage: One rule per module, generated from modules.php: must not depend on the other module namespaces; Framework\ is allowed; published domain event classes and consumer-owned interfaces are allow-listed.
One layer per module with no dependency between module layers; Framework\ allowed from every layer; published domain event classes and consumer-owned interfaces are allow-listed.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ISO-001 (no cross-module imports).

entries.rule: Cross-module collaboration **MUST** go through a contract (interface) defined by the consuming module and implemented by the providing module, or through a published domain event, never through any other import; a module **MUST** own its copy of any value object it needs, and a slice **MUST** live in the module that owns the capability.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ISO-002, ISO-003, ISO-004, ARCH-011 (contract or event, consumer defines it, no shared kernel, slice in the owning context).

entries.rule: Cross-module references **MUST** be plain columns holding the other module's id, never a Doctrine association (`ManyToOne`, `OneToMany`, `OneToOne`, `ManyToMany`) to another module's entity and never a database foreign key across modules.

checks.coverage: The association target is an import of another module, so the module rules catch it. A cross-module foreign key in a migration is not covered.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ISO-005, PERS-004 (cross-module references are plain ids).

entries.rule: Data another module owns but this module needs at runtime **MUST** be materialized on this module's own table and kept in sync by an event listener, not fetched across modules per request; a call through a consumer-owned contract (SYM-102) and a read-only query under SYM-074 are the two exceptions to materializing.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ISO-008 (materialize data you need from another module).

entries.rule: Once a second application exists, application namespaces **MUST NOT** import from each other, in either direction.
applies_to: projects with two or more applications (for example a public site and an admin panel)

checks.coverage: One rule per application namespace, both directions.

examples.bad:
namespace Admin\Member;

use Web\Member\MemberRepository; // another application's class

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ISO-009 (applications do not import each other).

entries.rule: Once a second application exists, an application **MUST NOT** register a listener on another application's event (by attribute, tag or string FQCN).
applies_to: projects with two or more applications (for example a public site and an admin panel)

checks.coverage: The event class import in the listener is caught by the application-import rule. A string FQCN in a tag or attribute argument is not covered.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ISO-011 (no cross-application event subscriptions).

entries.rule: Once a second application exists, every side effect of an application's action **MUST** be handled by that application's own listeners, and an application **MUST NOT** dispatch another application's domain events to reuse its cascades.
applies_to: projects with two or more applications (for example a public site and an admin panel)

examples.good:
namespace Admin\Order;

$this->eventBus->dispatch(new OrderPlacedByStaff($orderId)); // Admin's own event, Admin's own listeners

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ISO-012 (own side effects, no reuse of another application's cascades).

entries.rule: Tests **MUST** use PHPUnit with the `#[Test]` attribute; a test that boots the kernel **MUST** extend `KernelTestCase` or `WebTestCase`; Pest **MUST NOT** be used.

checks.coverage: Flags a Pest-style it(...) closure test and a test method that lacks #[Test].
Flags a kernel-booting test class that does not extend KernelTestCase or WebTestCase.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-001 (PHPUnit, `#[Test]`, project TestCase, no Pest).

entries.rule: Pure domain tests **SHOULD** extend `PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase`, so they run without booting the kernel or the database.
entries.why: they run without booting the kernel or the database
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-002 (pure domain tests extend the plain TestCase).

entries.rule: Tests that touch the database **MUST** isolate state with Foundry's `#[ResetDatabase]` attribute on the test class and the `FoundryExtension` PHPUnit extension registered; the `ResetDatabase` and `Factories` traits are deprecated since Foundry 2.9.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-004 (database refreshed per test).

entries.rule: Test data **MUST** come from factories and their named states; a hand-built `new Entity(...)` followed by `persist()` where a state exists is a violation.

checks.coverage: Custom rule: flags persist( in a test class; it over-flags legitimate setup.

examples.good: $order = OrderFactory::new()->shipped()->create();

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-005 (test data from factories).

entries.rule: Every entity **MUST** ship a test factory: a `final` class extending `PersistentObjectFactory`, with named state methods for each lifecycle position.

checks.coverage: Flags a factory class that is not final.

examples.bad:
// no factory: every test builds the entity by hand
$order = new Order($id, 'ORD-1', OrderStatus::Placed);

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: PERS-006 (every model ships a factory).

entries.rule: Tests **MAY** fetch services from the test container (`static::getContainer()->get(...)`); production code still never fetches services from the container.
applies_to: PHPUnit tests extending KernelTestCase or WebTestCase
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-006 (facades and helpers allowed in tests).

entries.rule: Controller happy-path tests **MUST** assert the full response structure (every key of the `*Resource`), not a spot-check.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-008 (assert the full response structure).

entries.rule: Every `#[Assert\...]` constraint on a `*Request` **MUST** have a `WebTestCase` test that triggers it and asserts the 422.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-009 (every validation rule has a test).

entries.rule: Any test that creates, updates or deletes data **MUST** assert the resulting database state with `assertSame`, re-reading through an `EntityManager` that was cleared first.

checks.coverage: Flags assertEquals in a test class; it over-flags legitimate loose comparisons.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-010 (assert database state, strict comparison).

entries.rule: A handler that dispatches a domain event **MUST** be tested by asserting the event class and its properties on `event.bus` (`InteractsWithMessenger` from zenstruck/messenger-test, or `InMemoryTransport::getSent()` for an event routed to a transport).

examples.bad:
$this->commandBus->dispatch(new CancelOrderCommand($id));
self::assertSame(OrderStatus::Cancelled, $this->statusOf($id)); // the event is never checked

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-011 (event dispatch tested with a fake).

entries.rule: Side effects **MUST** be asserted (`assertEmailCount()`, `assertQueuedEmailCount()`, the notifier assertions, `InMemoryTransport::getSent()`).

examples.bad:
$client->jsonRequest('POST', '/api/sign-up', ['email' => 'ada@example.com']);
self::assertResponseStatusCodeSame(201); // the welcome email is never checked

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-012 (side effects asserted).

entries.rule: Every product `*Exception` **MUST** have a test that triggers it and asserts the HTTP status and message.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-013 (every business-rule exception tested).

entries.rule: Every authenticated endpoint **MUST** have a test asserting the unauthenticated response, and every owned-resource endpoint a test asserting failure for a non-owner.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-014 (401 unauthenticated, failure for a non-owner).

entries.rule: Controller tests **SHOULD** assert the dispatched command against an in-memory bus instead of running the handler.

examples.bad:
$client->jsonRequest('POST', '/api/orders', ['sku' => 'A1']);
self::assertResponseStatusCodeSame(201); // the real handler ran, with its database writes
